talks.title: Wendy Nather - Keynote: A Tabletop As Big As the World
talks.teaser: Evaluates wendy Nather - Keynote: A Tabletop As Big As the World and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Wendy Nather delivers the NorthSec keynote "A Tabletop As Big As the World," sharing lessons from decades of incident response on building organizational resilience.

Key Topics: Pre-approved communication templates for breach notification; decision frameworks for incident leadership; procurement challenges during active incidents; and cross-departmental incident preparation including insider threat scenarios.

Technical Details: Nather recommends pre-negotiating communication templates with legal teams and establishing decision frameworks before incidents occur. She shares anecdotes including imaging an inspector general's machine after hours and tabletop exercises for unexpected insider scenarios.

Takeaways: Incident response success depends on preparation, not improvisation. Organizations should pre-approve templates, establish decision authority, and practice scenarios involving unexpected personnel.

talks.title: François Labrèche - How not to do ML
talks.teaser: Analyzes françois Labrèche - How not to do ML and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Problem Statement

François Labrèche of Sophos presents pitfalls in ML-based exploit prediction for vulnerability management. With over 40,000 CVEs yearly and few actually exploited, a classifier could help prioritize patching—but improper feature encoding can silently destroy real-world performance.

Model Design

The team builds a random forest on NVD metadata: LDA topic vectors from CVE descriptions, description length, product and reference counts, CVSS features, publication dates, and online mention counts from Reddit, Pastebin, Telegram, and dark web forums via Flare. Labels indicate whether public exploits exist in Exploit-DB, Packet Storm, or GitHub PoCs.

Encouraging Offline Metrics

Ten-fold cross-validation reports 93% accuracy and 83% recall, suggesting production readiness. The speaker warns such metrics can mislead because encoding mistakes often surface only during live deployment on newly published CVEs.

Lessons on Feature Selection

The talk title frames the presentation as how not to do machine learning: even standard pipelines need careful feature design. Labrèche planned to demonstrate revised modeling and April live predictions, emphasizing validation beyond offline cross-validation scores.

talks.title: Unlinkable Digital Life Crypto's Privacy Solutions
talks.teaser: Analyzes unlinkable Digital Life Cryptos Privacy Solutions and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
The Unlinkability Problem

Electronic credentials leave correlation handles—PII fields, public keys, and signatures—that let issuers, advertisers, or colluding verifiers track where someone went online. The speaker warns digital life becomes a “where’s Waldo” game built on Web 2.0 tracking business models.

Correlation Handles in Practice

Unlike paper IDs shown once at a bar, digital tokens repeatedly expose stable identifiers. Even without requesting a new token, log analysis can reconstruct a person’s day from fingerprinted presentations across services.

Cryptographic Countermeasures

Unlinkable signatures address this through blind signatures or proof-based credential schemes that randomize values at issuance or presentation. Selective disclosure can use stronger black-box cryptography than simple hash-based redaction, preventing salt brute force and enumeration.

Privacy Outcome

When deployed correctly, colluding or malicious verifiers cannot link presentations across contexts, preserving transactional privacy while still proving authorization.

talks.title: Christian Paquin - Enhancing Identity Credential Privacy with Zero-Knowledge Proofs
talks.teaser: Outlines christian Paquin - Enhancing Identity Credential Privacy with Zero-Knowledge Proofs and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Privacy motivation

Christian Paquin at NorthSec revisits zero-knowledge ideas from his early Zero Knowledge Systems career, now resonating alongside zero trust. He focuses on minimizing data disclosed when digital identity credentials replace physical IDs such as Quebec driver's licenses used for age checks.

Over-disclosure today

Showing a full license online or to websites exposes name, address, and residence data beyond what verifiers need, and issuers learn where credentials are used when attributes are fetched on demand via OAuth-style JWT flows.

Selective disclosure credentials

He contrasts long-lived X.509 certificates with ubiquitous signed JWTs that cannot be redacted without breaking signatures. New ISO mobile driver's license and SD-JWT profiles hash salted attributes so holders reveal only chosen pre-images, enabling minimal claims such as boolean over-18 without leaking birthdates, while keeping issuer-backed authenticity.

talks.title: Tammy Harper - Persōna Theory: Infiltration and Deception of Emerging Threat Groups
talks.teaser: Details tammy Harper - Persōna Theory: Infiltration and Deception of Emerging Threat Groups and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
## Overview
Tammy Harper applies Carl Jung's persona theory to undercover operations inside ransomware affiliate ecosystems at NorthSec.

## RaaS Economics and Recruitment
Affiliate programs commonly split revenue 70/30 to 90/10 in favor of operators. Groups like Van Helsing produce polished recruitment videos to attract affiliates—a competitive, creative underground marketing arms race.

## Operational Case Study
Researchers built credible personas, joined the Slav group, then pivoted toward A73/Bashi by claiming prior earnings and offering recycled initial access tied to trending phishing kits—mirroring how affiliates prove value.

## Takeaways
Understanding persona, financial incentives, and group-specific slang is essential for threat-intel infiltration—and defenders should study these recruitment patterns to spot insider-risk precursors.
